content.comment_body: I'm experiencing an issue where a message is not displayed on the [product_name] operator panel when using a flag as the ON/OFF status, even though it appears correctly on the [product_name] controller. The message destination is set to 'Both.' When I switch the flag to an input or output, the message displays correctly on both devices. Equipment used includes two [product_name] devices with [article_no] and firmware [version_no] in a master/client network, along with a [product_name] panel ([article_no], firmware [version_no]), using [product_name] software [version_no]. I'm not sure if the firmware is the latest. Is this a known issue? Any advice would be appreciated.

Hello, This is a curious issue. I attempted a similar setup and couldn't get the ON/OFF status of a message triggered by an M-bit flag. In my [product_name] software ([version_no]), only inputs and outputs work for this purpose, so it's unexpected that you could select a flag. A possible workaround is to use an unused output as a substitute for the flag; for example, if you only use the base unit, outputs above a certain point are available. Update: The hardware version matters—I used [version_no] which displays only input/output status. It seems your [version_no] panel may not be up-to-date with all features, or it's a limitation of that hardware release. Your panel's release date suggests it's older than your controller version. Perhaps someone can confirm the latest operator panel version or replicate this issue. For now, the workaround is recommended.

Hi, There are indeed different firmware versions for the [product_name] panel. Firmware version [version_no] is fully compatible with the [product_name] controller [version_no], and [version_no] is fully compatible with the newer [product_name] controllers. Using an older panel version with a newer controller may result in missing features or issues. Regards,

Thanks for your suggestions. I managed a workaround by analyzing other logic states and finding a combination that matched the required machine state, though this approach was more complex than simply using a flag input. Unfortunately, I don't have enough spare outputs to use that solution. There's another issue—one particular message in the program stopped working even though it references a local input, while others configured the same way work fine. Rebuilding the circuit didn't help, but changing the reference to a different input restores functionality. I suspect the problem comes from either the new [product_name] operator panel I bought recently, or the controllers I've had for a while. I have contacted [company_name] technical support, hoping to resolve this soon. I'll share any updates. Thanks again.
[user_name], Thanks for your information. Do you know how I can confirm if I have the [product_name] panel with the required firmware version?
Hello, On most [company_name] devices, the firmware and version information is usually printed on the casing. Do you know what the identifiers for the [product_name] modules mean? Regards,

We've resolved the issue by upgrading to a [product_name] panel with firmware [version_no], and the problem no longer occurs. Thanks to everyone for your help. By the way, I'm surprised [company_name] technical support couldn't provide up-to-date information on the latest firmware versions for both the controller and operator panel.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered inconsistent message display behavior involving flags used as message triggers: messages with flags show correctly on the [product_name] controller but not on the corresponding operator panel. Inputs and outputs work as expected for triggering messages on both devices. The issue was traced to firmware compatibility between panel and controller; upgrading the operator panel firmware resolved it, demonstrating the need for matching versions to ensure expected functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that message display logic should be consistent between the controller and the operator panel, regardless of whether flags, inputs, or outputs are used as message triggers, provided compatible hardware and firmware versions are in use.
